title: Protocell formation on micrometeorites
task: Understanding lipid self-assembly on extraterrestrial particle surfaces for protocell formation
key_results: Lipids autonomously form spherical compartments and nanotubes on micrometeorite surfaces; certain lipid compositions preferentially adhere to micrometeorites versus natural sand particles
comments: The mechanism by which surface energy drives transformation is proposed but not quantitatively characterized; actual prebiotic relevance depends on whether such particles were abundant and accessible in early Earth environments.

model_io.model: Lipid self-assembly system

hypotheses.hypothesis: Surface energy of micrometeorites drives lipid assembly preferentially over natural sand
hypotheses.result: Certain lipid compositions showed enhanced assembly on micrometeorites; elemental composition, surface texture, and cleanness contribute to differential behavior

title: Adaptive low-rank variational quantum algorithm for simulating dissipative dynamics in photosynthetic complexes
task: Simulating photosynthetic light harvesting dynamics on quantum hardware
key_results: Low-rank variational quantum algorithm achieves polynomial O(n^2.5Rd) scaling with fidelities 0.87–0.95 (5–12 chromophores) and 0.932±0.001 on IBM Heron; computational crossover at N=14 chromophores favors quantum over classical methods; energy transfer timescales agree with experiment within 3%
comments: The work elegantly demonstrates NISQ viability for a realistic biophysics problem, though current fidelities still leave room for improvement and the crossover point is modest.

model_io.model: Low-rank variational quantum algorithm (LR-VQA)
Classical benchmarks (HOPS, Meso-HOPS, Davydov)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Low-rank tensor compression enables tractable quantum simulation of photosynthetic complexes beyond classical reach
hypotheses.result: LR-VQA scaled to 12 chromophores with high fidelity; classical density-matrix methods prohibitive beyond ~15 chromophores

hypotheses.hypothesis: NISQ devices can simulate photosynthetic energy transfer accurately despite realistic noise
hypotheses.result: 7-site FMO complex on IBM Heron achieved fidelity 0.932±0.001; energy timescales within 3% of experiment

title: Fluorescent probes as markers of cell envelope structure and function in halophilic archaea
task: Evaluating fluorescent probes for assessing cell envelope structure and function in extreme halophilic archaea
key_results: Propidium iodide showed unreliable behavior with false double-labeling; alamarBlue and resazurin are compatible redox markers; MitoTracker Orange-CMTMRos and Rhodamine 123 suitable for membrane potential measurement in high-salt conditions
comments: The systematic incompatibility assessment is methodologically sound but would benefit from mechanistic explanations for why certain probes fail in halophilic conditions.

model_io.model: Halophilic archaeal cell envelope system

hypotheses.hypothesis: Standard fluorescent probes are incompatible with extreme halophilic conditions and extremophile physiology
hypotheses.result: Propidium iodide unreliable with double-labeling artifacts; probe performance depends critically on growth phase, medium composition, and exposure time

hypotheses.hypothesis: Redox and membrane potential markers work effectively in saturated salt environments
hypotheses.result: alamarBlue, resazurin, MitoTracker Orange-CMTMRos, and Rhodamine 123 validated for bulk and cell-specific applications in haloarchaea

title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics-based drug screening platform for focal cortical dysplasia
task: Integrate single-nucleus transcriptomics with drug screening to identify therapeutics for focal cortical dysplasia
key_results: Single-nucleus RNA-seq of 49 neocortical specimens (FCDI-III) identified prominent transcriptional alterations in astrocytes and vascular cells; vascular-associated signatures consistently observed across FCD subtypes suggesting convergent pathology; Connectivity Map integration prioritized 20 compounds; four candidates (Betamethasone, Lodamin, Valproxam, Licochalcone A) reduced seizure-like activity in vivo in FCD models and mTOR-driven FCD model
comments: Innovative transcriptome-guided platform bridging multicellular disease signatures to therapeutics; primary focus on non-neuronal populations is underexplored given neuronal subtype heterogeneity.

model_io.model: Single-nucleus RNA-seq from 49 human neocortical FCD specimens; in vivo FCD models and seizure phenotyping
inputs: candidate compounds (Betamethasone, Lodamin, Valproxam, Licochalcone A)
outputs: seizure-like activity (behavioral assays, local field potential)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vascular and astrocytic dysfunction represent a convergent disease feature across FCD subtypes
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; vascular-associated transcriptional signatures consistently identified across FCDI-III subtypes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Compounds targeting cell-type-resolved transcriptional signatures can reduce seizure activity in FCD models
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; four prioritized compounds reduced seizure-like activity in vivo

title: Inhibiting CXCL12/CXCR4 axis enhances T cell activity in gastric cancer
task: Establish CXCL12/CXCR4 axis role in M2 macrophage polarization and immune evasion in gastric cancer
key_results: Single-cell RNA-seq revealed increased M2-polarized TAM population in murine GC; CXCL12/CXCR4 axis mediates CAF-TAM communication driving M2 polarization; CAFs induced M2 polarization through CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling in vitro; CXCR4 silencing reduced M2 macrophages and PD-L1 expression, enhanced T cell proliferation, and slowed tumor growth; M2 macrophages suppress T cells via PD-L1/PD-1 axis
comments: Comprehensive immunophenotyping identifying CAF-TAM-T cell axis in GC immune evasion; therapeutic targeting requires managing potential off-target CXCR4 inhibition in normal tissues.

model_io.model: Murine GC model with single-cell RNA-seq; in vitro CAF-macrophage coculture; tumor-bearing mice with CXCR4 silencing

hypotheses.hypothesis: CXCL12/CXCR4 axis drives CAF-mediated M2 macrophage polarization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CAF-derived CXCL12 induces M2 polarization in macrophages via CXCR4

hypotheses.hypothesis: M2 macrophage polarization via CXCL12/CXCR4 axis promotes immune evasion through PD-L1-mediated T cell suppression
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CXCR4 inhibition reduces M2 macrophages and PD-L1, enhancing T cell proliferation and tumor control

title: K-Ras controls asymmetric cell divisions from the primary cilium
task: Determine role of K-Ras4B localization to primary cilium in controlling asymmetric cell division and differentiation
key_results: K-Ras4B but not N-/H-Ras localizes to primary cilium via PDE6D chaperone; ciliary K-Ras4B sustains ciliation during differentiation in skeletal muscle stem cells, restricting commitment during asymmetric division; oncogenic K-Ras4B-G12C and modulation of ciliary abundance perturb differentiation; in vivo zebrafish data shows K-Ras4B controls ciliation-dependent heart looping
comments: Novel compartmentalization of Ras signaling to cilium with isoform specificity; findings may explain RASopathy-ciliopathy phenotypic overlap, though tissue-specific roles require further investigation.

model_io.model: Skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells with K-Ras4B manipulation and mathematical modeling
Zebrafish embryos with K-Ras4B modulation during early development

hypotheses.hypothesis: K-Ras4B localizes to the primary cilium and is catalytically active there
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; K-Ras4B localizes via PDE6D; B-Raf, MEK, and ERK detected at cilium base or inside cilium

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ciliary K-Ras4B sustains ciliation to restrict stem cell commitment during asymmetric division
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; K-Ras4B modulation alters ciliation and differentiation; oncogenic variant perturbs both

title: ENO2 sustains cancer stemness and metastatic competence through a phosphoenolpyruvate-dependent metabolic axis in triple-negative breast cancer
task: Establish ENO2-driven phosphoenolpyruvate metabolic axis in TNBC stemness and metastasis
key_results: High ENO2 expression correlated with advanced grade and poor outcomes in TNBC; ENO2 depletion impaired glycolysis, OXPHOS, migration, invasion, CSC frequency, tumor growth, and pulmonary metastasis; exogenous PEP or pyruvate restored CSC traits in ENO2-deficient cells; reconstitution required catalytically active ENO2; PKM2 perturbation partially blunted PEP-mediated rescue; POMHEX enolase inhibitor phenocopied genetic ENO2 loss
comments: Elegant metabolic mechanistic work linking glycolytic enzyme activity to stemness; PKM2-independent PEP-responsive mechanisms suggest additional targets remain unidentified.

model_io.model: TNBC cell lines with ENO2 manipulation; orthotopic xenografts

hypotheses.hypothesis: ENO2 catalytic activity sustains CSC properties and metastatic competence via PEP-dependent metabolism
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; catalytically active but not catalytically impaired ENO2 restores CSC traits and invasiveness

hypotheses.hypothesis: PEP-PKM2 axis mediates ENO2-dependent CSC regulation
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed; PKM2 depletion blunts PEP-mediated rescue but not pyruvate-mediated rescue, suggesting PKM2-independent mechanisms

title: Role of the trophoblastic BMP7-TGM2 axis in the pathogenesis and prevention of preeclampsia
task: Define BMP7-TGM2 regulatory axis controlling trophoblast invasion and preeclampsia prevention
key_results: Single-cell RNA-seq revealed coordinated BMP7 downregulation and TGM2 upregulation in PE placentas; BMP7 promotes trophoblast migration/invasion by suppressing TGM2 via ALK2/3-SMAD1/5/9 signaling; trophoblast organoid models confirmed TGM2 anti-invasive role; recombinant BMP7 ameliorated PE symptoms in Ad sFlt-1 mouse model; BMP7 administration reduced placental Tgm2
comments: Integrated single-cell genomics with functional studies and in vivo validation; protective BMP7 effects in vivo likely involve mechanisms beyond TGM2 suppression alone.

model_io.model: Placental tissue single-cell RNA-seq (PE vs normotensive); immortalized and primary human trophoblasts; trophoblast organoid models
Ad sFlt-1-induced PE mouse model with recombinant BMP7 administration

hypotheses.hypothesis: BMP7 suppresses TGM2 in trophoblasts to promote migration and invasion
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; BMP7 promotes trophoblast migration/invasion via ALK2/3-SMAD pathway-mediated TGM2 suppression

hypotheses.hypothesis: TGM2 upregulation in PE impairs trophoblast invasion and placental development
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; TGM2 overexpression reduces trophoblast invasion in organoid models; PE placentas show elevated TGM2

title: Intrinsic polyunsaturated fatty acid synthesis capacity dictates ferroptosis sensitivity under restricted arachidonic acid availability
task: Identify PUFA biosynthetic capacity as determinant of ferroptosis sensitivity under arachidonic acid limitation
key_results: H1299 cells (KEAP1-WT, ferroptosis-sensitive) have impaired PUFA biosynthesis but maintain ferroptosis sensitivity via exogenous AA; A549 cells (KEAP1-mutant) retain ferroptosis sensitivity under AA-limited B27 conditions via endogenous PUFA synthesis; FADS2 inhibition or ELOVL5 deletion phenocopy H1299 sensitivity loss; AA supplementation reverses resistance
comments: Important demonstration that intrinsic lipid synthetic capacity, not just KEAP1 status, determines ferroptosis vulnerability; physiological relevance hinges on actual in vivo lipid availability.

model_io.model: Human lung adenocarcinoma cell lines (H1299, A549) under variable lipid media conditions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Intrinsic PUFA biosynthetic capacity determines ferroptosis sensitivity under AA limitation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; A549 (high PUFA synthesis) remain sensitive under B27; H1299 (low synthesis) become resistant; FADS2/ELOVL5 perturbation phenocopies sensitivity loss

hypotheses.hypothesis: Exogenous AA can compensate for impaired endogenous PUFA synthesis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; AA supplementation restores ferroptosis sensitivity in FADS2-inhibited or ELOVL5-deleted cells

title: Colorectal cancer co-opts an epidermal wound healing program during metastasis to generate disseminated tumor cells
task: Identify cellular state enabling colorectal cancer metastatic dissemination
key_results: DTCs transiently express wound-healing keratin KRT17, lose cancer stem cell markers, show reduced EZH2 activity and activated YAP signaling; state is reversible upon organ colonization; KRT17+ cells localize to invasive fronts of primary CRCs
comments: Remarkable discovery of phenotypic plasticity across developmental lineages; the transient, reversible nature of the DTC state may complicate therapeutic targeting.

model_io.model: Serial orthotopic transplantation of patient-derived CRC organoids

hypotheses.hypothesis: DTCs adopt a wound-healing program distinct from cancer stem cell state
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; DTCs express KRT17 and wound-inducible keratins while losing CSC features

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reduced EZH2 activity and YAP activation drive the DTC state
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; mechanistic association identified between epigenetic and signaling changes

title: Simulated microgravity with physiological shear reveals endothelial disruption in a dual-stimulus bioreactor
task: Assess endothelial dysfunction under combined simulated microgravity and physiological shear stress
key_results: 16h dual-stimulus exposure induced cytoskeletal disorganization, loss of VE-cadherin junctions, and altered secretion of Angpt-2, VEGF, PDGF in HUVECs compared to individual stimulus controls
comments: Well-designed bioreactor system bridging static and flow models; however, 16h timeframe may not capture delayed adaptive responses to microgravity.

model_io.model: Dual-stimulus benchtop bioreactor with simulated microgravity and laminar shear (3 dyn/cm²)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Combined microgravity and shear stress disrupts endothelial homeostasis more severely than individual stressors
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dual-stimulus induced cytoskeletal disorganization and junction loss absent in single-stimulus controls

title: Comprehensive analysis of miRNA expression, secretion profile, and functional network during myogenesis in response to spaceflight
task: Analyze miRNA expression and secretion changes during myogenesis in spaceflight conditions
key_results: Comprehensive profiling identified spaceflight-responsive miRNAs in myoblast myogenesis with distinct expression and secretion patterns; qRT-PCR validation in disuse atrophy model confirmed relevance; miRNA mimics confirmed regulatory roles in target gene expression and myoblast proliferation/differentiation; spaceflight may regulate miRNA secretion/retention via RNA-binding proteins (RBPs); muscle-derived miRNAs implicated in systemic adaptation
comments: Solid characterization of muscle miRNA responses to spaceflight; mechanistic role of RBPs in miRNA secretion remains to be fully elucidated.

model_io.model: Mouse myoblasts during myogenesis in spaceflight-simulated conditions (actual spaceflight samples) and disuse-induced atrophy model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spaceflight perturbs miRNA expression and secretion during myogenesis, contributing to muscle atrophy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; miRNA deregulation observed in spaceflight myoblasts and disuse atrophy model; miRNA mimics modulate target expression and myoblast phenotype

hypotheses.hypothesis: RBPs regulate miRNA secretion in response to spaceflight
hypotheses.result: Supported; spaceflight may modulate RBP expression to alter miRNA secretion/retention

title: GATA1 silencing restrains granulosa cell ferroptosis through downregulation of TFRC in polycystic ovary syndrome
task: Establish GATA1–TFRC axis in granulosa cell ferroptosis and PCOS pathogenesis
key_results: PCOS mice showed elevated ovarian GATA1; GATA1 overexpression in KGN cells increased lipid ROS, malondialdehyde, iron, and reduced glutathione—all reversed by ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1; GATA1 knockdown alleviated Erastin-induced ferroptosis; GATA1 directly binds TFRC promoter to activate transcription; TFRC overexpression counteracted GATA1 knockdown protection
comments: Well-integrated mechanism linking transcription factor to iron homeostasis in granulosa cells; therapeutic targeting of GATA1 pathway warrants caution regarding potential off-target effects on hematopoiesis.

model_io.model: In vivo PCOS model (DHEA-induced mice) and KGN cell line

hypotheses.hypothesis: GATA1 promotes granulosa cell ferroptosis through TFRC-mediated iron accumulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; GATA1 directly activates TFRC transcription; TFRC overexpression reverses ferroptosis protection from GATA1 knockdown

hypotheses.hypothesis: GATA1 overexpression drives ferroptosis in PCOS granulosa cells
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; GATA1 increases ROS, malondialdehyde, and iron in KGN cells; effects blocked by ferroptosis inhibitor

title: Extracellular vesicles from inflammatory-primed stromal cells reduce in vitro inflammation in Sandhoff disease model
task: Evaluate anti-inflammatory efficacy of inflammatory-primed MSC-derived extracellular vesicles (IFEVs) in Sandhoff disease model
key_results: IFEVs reduced IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β in SD neuronal-mixed glia with downregulation of NF-κB/p65 and NLRP3 and upregulation of arginase 1; in SD PBMC, IFEVs increased regulatory T cell proportion and Treg/T-effector ratio without cytotoxicity; effects observed within 48h of treatment
comments: Promising immunomodulatory strategy combining enzyme-restoring and anti-inflammatory approaches; feline model validity for human translational work warrants confirmation.

model_io.model: Feline Sandhoff disease model with in vitro neuroinflammation and immune assays
inputs: MSC-derived extracellular vesicles from inflammatory-primed (IFEVs) vs non-primed MSCs

hypotheses.hypothesis: IFEVs reduce neuroinflammation in SD model by activating anti-inflammatory pathways
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; IFEVs downregulated NF-κB/p65 and NLRP3 signaling and upregulated arginase 1

hypotheses.hypothesis: IFEVs promote regulatory T cell differentiation and suppress T-effector responses
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; IFEVs increased Treg proportion and Treg/T-effector ratio in SD PBMC

title: ATP6AP2 in osteoblasts couples cortical bone matrix remodeling to osteocyte maturation via MMP14 activation in mice
task: Establish role of ATP6AP2 in osteocyte maturation and cortical bone organization
key_results: Osteoblast-specific Atp6ap2 deletion increased cortical bone mass with woven bone phenotype, impaired osteocyte maturation/survival, and abnormal distribution; MMP14 identified as key downstream effector; ATP6AP2–MMP14 axis controls woven-to-lamellar transition
comments: Novel mechanistic link between vesicular acidification and bone matrix remodeling; translational relevance depends on whether similar pathway operates in human osteoblasts.

model_io.model: Atp6ap2OCN-Cre transgenic mice with osteoblast-lineage-specific deletion

hypotheses.hypothesis: ATP6AP2 is essential for osteocyte differentiation and cortical bone organization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Atp6ap2 deletion impairs osteocyte maturation and generates woven bone

hypotheses.hypothesis: MMP14 mediates ATP6AP2 effects on bone remodeling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; MMP14 expression in Atp6ap2-deficient cells partially rescues cortical bone phenotype

title: Contribution of cohesins STAG1 and STAG2 to preimplantation development in mice
task: Determine functional requirements of cohesin variants STAG1 and STAG2 in preimplantation development
key_results: Both STAG1 and STAG2 are maternally stored in oocytes; maternal STAG1 persists beyond 2-cell stage while STAG2 accumulation depends on zygotic transcription; despite different STAG1:STAG2 ratios between epiblast and primitive endoderm lineages, both variants are individually dispensable for preimplantation viability if the other is present; STAG2 absence increases zygotic DNA damage and perturbs blastocyst transcription
comments: Elegant dissection of cohesin variant redundancy during early development; early DNA damage without lethality suggests compensatory mechanisms that break down by mid-gestation.

model_io.model: Murine preimplantation embryos with selective STAG1 or STAG2 deletion; oocytes and zygotes
outputs: STAG1 and STAG2 protein levels (maternal vs zygotic)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Either STAG1 or STAG2 is sufficient for preimplantation development if the other variant is present
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; single STAG variant deletion compatible with preimplantation development

hypotheses.hypothesis: STAG2 deficiency causes early DNA damage without compromising preimplantation viability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; STAG2 absence increases zygotic DNA damage but permits continued development through blastocyst stage

title: Oxidative base damage to telomeres sensitizes cancer cells to ATR inhibition
task: Enhance ATR inhibitor efficacy in cancer via telomeric oxidative damage
key_results: ATR/CHK1/WEE1 inhibition after 8-oxo-guanine induction reduced cancer cell viability at markedly lower doses than required for non-cancerous cells; mechanism involves insufficient RPA at damaged telomeres forcing S-phase progression with unrepaired damage
comments: Elegant demonstration that targeting a specific DNA lesion type can selectively sensitize cancer cells to checkpoint inhibition, though clinical translation requires addressing RPA bioavailability.

model_io.model: Cancer cell lines with 8-oxo-guanine induction at telomeres

hypotheses.hypothesis: Telomeric 8-oxo-guanine renders cancer cells dependent on ATR-CHK1-WEE1 checkpoint signaling

hypotheses.hypothesis: Insufficient RPA at damaged telomeres forces unrepaired progression through S-phase
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; RPA depletion at telomeres correlates with checkpoint bypass and prolonged mitosis
